subject.title: backup create stalls on large installations (4GB+ .openclaw dir)

question: What restore-safe core behavior should `openclaw backup create` support for large state directories: native smart/custom exclusions, a minimal completion/error/progress fix, or a documented coarse-backup boundary?
rationale: The bug is concrete, but choosing default exclusions, protected backup contents, and whether to solve the stall through scope control or archive reliability changes affects restore completeness and security, and an open closing PR already claims the implementation path.

options.title: Review or replace linked native exclusions
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a narrower replacement to settle smart/custom excludes, protected paths, manifest behavior, docs, and large-state proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Split reliability first
options.body: Track completion, clear failure, progress, and temp cleanup separately while leaving native exclude-pattern policy to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/40786.

options.title: Defer native exclusions
options.body: Keep core backups coarse, document limits and workarounds, and point optional backup strategies to plugin or ClawHub paths only after an explicit maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Review or replace linked native exclusions
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 or a narrower replacement to settle smart/custom excludes, protected paths, manifest behavior, docs, and large-state proof before closing this issue.
